content.title: About
content.content: Walnuts are the edible seeds of the walnut tree (Juglans regia). Raw halves have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture. They are eaten raw, and also used in baking, desserts, salads, and as an ingredient in various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Walnuts belong to the nut family and are relatives of chestnuts and hazelnuts.
They contain higher levels of polyphenols than most other nuts.
Walnuts are a rich source of omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for cardiovascular health.
Historically, walnuts have symbolized wisdom and longevity in many cultures.
Harvest season is autumn, after which the nuts are dried and shelled.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Walnuts provide alpha‑linolenic acid, which helps lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Antioxidant source
items.content: They contain vitamin E, polyphenols, and melatonin that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports brain function
items.content: Polyphenols and omega‑3s improve cognition and memory.

items.title: Contains magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals support normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: They help maintain satiety and regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Walnuts can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Because of their energy density, they should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Whole nuts and large pieces can be dangerous for young children.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Oxalates may contribute to kidney stone formation in predisposed persons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Walnuts can be eaten as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, salads, baked goods, and sauces. Raw halves are convenient for granola or as a garnish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store walnuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts with a rancid smell.
